headline: Seven majors under their 200-day lines, but longs are crowded and paying for the privilege
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's uniform: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE and ADA are all trading below their 200-day moving averages, none showing a golden cross. Every one of them also sits deep off its 12-month high, from BTC's -49.6% to ADA's -82.5%. When the whole board agrees like this, you're not picking through mixed signals asset by asset, you're reading one macro backdrop: a market that hasn't repaired its long-term trend anywhere.

Momentum tells a more layered story. RSI-14 readings are clustered in neutral territory (BTC 44.5, ETH 50.9, SOL 42.2, XRP 41.7, DOGE 39.6, ADA 51.9, BNB 57.6), nobody oversold, nobody overbought. But MACD splits the group: BTC, ETH, SOL and XRP sit below their signal lines, while BNB, DOGE and ADA sit above. That's a real divergence, smaller-cap momentum quietly turning up while the majors still carry downside momentum beneath a downtrend. Worth watching whether that gap closes or widens.

Positioning is where the tension sharpens. BTC funding is running +5.8% annualized and SOL +2.5%, meaning longs are paying shorts to hold their bets, a sign the crowd is leaning bullish even with price under trend. Long/short account ratios confirm it: every asset with data shows more longs than shorts, from BTC's 2.08 up to DOGE's 5.45. That's a crowded long book. And crowded longs get punished: BTC liquidations over roughly 23 hours show $12.07M in longs wiped out against just $601K in shorts; ETH shows $14.98M in longs against $1.17M in shorts over about 22 hours. The boat is full on one side and taking on water.

Flows add another layer of disagreement. The BTC spot ETF printed -$87.9M on 31 Jul, but the five-session net is +$116M, and same_direction_days sits at just 1, meaning that single day broke whatever streak preceded it, not evidence of a fresh trend either way. ETH ETFs are smaller and softer: -$4.5M on the day, -$3.5M over five sessions, same single-day flag. On the whale side, the 24-hour tape shows $54.9M in BTC moving onto exchanges (into Binance), consistent with the label 'onto exchanges,' while the broader weekly readings ($689M off, -$393M on, $361M off, $925M off) show the week's dominant pull has been off exchanges, not on. Today's move onto exchanges is a small counter-current inside a week that's mostly leaned the other way. Stablecoin float is down 1.6% over 30 days and stablecoin buying power reads -$152.4M, both pointing to slightly less dry powder sitting on the sidelines right now, not more.

Sentiment sits at Fear & Greed 27, labeled Fear, which is actually mid-pack against its own 30-day range of 20 to 33, not a fresh extreme. That calibrates the mood: this isn't panic beyond what's already been priced this month. But it sits oddly next to a derivatives book that's crowded long and paying funding to stay there. Fear in the gauge, confidence in the leverage. That gap between what the crowd says and what the crowd's money is doing is the story worth sitting with today.

What to watch from here: any MACD cross back below signal in BNB, DOGE or ADA (closing that momentum divergence), a funding flip to negative on BTC or SOL (longs no longer willing to pay), an ETF same_direction_days reading that climbs past 1 in either direction, and whether the whale weekly series turns decisively onto exchanges rather than the mixed pattern seen in the last four readings.
